question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $35,$ the additive inverse of $23$ modulo $35$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $23$ modulo $35$ is the integer $0\le x<35$ such that

$$
x+23≡0\,(\text{mod}\,35).
$$

Notice that $-23+23≡0,$ so $x≡-23\,(\text{mod}\,35).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-23 & \,(\text{mod}\,35) \\  & ≡0-23 & \,(\text{mod}\,35) \\  & ≡35-23 & \,(\text{mod}\,35) \\  & ≡12 & \,(\text{mod}\,35)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $23$ modulo $35$ is $12.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
12+23≡35≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,35)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
